title: HfO2/SiO2 20-layer emissivity selective stack with refined thickness perturbation
scientific_hypothesis: A 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 dielectric stack with individually optimized thicknesses can achieve higher emissivity in 8000-13000 nm than in 3000-5000 nm on a Si substrate, and reducing perturbation bounds while increasing penalty weight will improve convergence stability without sacrificing target score.
design_principle: Recalled knowledge: Dielectric multilayers create wavelength-selective reflectance/transmittance through constructive and destructive interference. High-index HfO2 and low-index SiO2 form contrast pairs. Quarter-wave or non-quarter-wave thickness profiles can create bandpass or bandstop behavior. Emissivity equals absorptance per Kirchhoff's law for opaque substrates.
proposed_topology: air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Si substrate (20 layers total, alternating HfO2/SiO2 starting with HfO2)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 20 layers
soft_objectives: maintain physical validity of all candidates
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 20 (within 24-layer limit)
thicknesses in nanometer range suitable for deposition
theory_basis: Recalled: Emissivity equals absorptance for opaque materials per Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation
Recalled: Dielectric stacks create wavelength-selective interference patterns based on optical thickness (n×d)
Recalled: High index contrast between HfO2 and SiO2 enables strong spectral selectivity
Recalled: Non-quarter-wave thickness profiles can optimize for multi-band objectives better than periodic stacks
Recalled: Reducing optimization step size improves local convergence at cost of exploration range
expected_advantages: Finer perturbation bounds reduce risk of jumping away from good local optima
Higher penalty weight enforces smoother thickness transitions between iterations
20 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for spectral shaping without excessive complexity
Alternating HfO2/SiO2 provides maximum index contrast from available materials
known_risks: Uncertain whether HfO2 and SiO2 extinction coefficients are negligible in 3-13 micron range - would need measured n/k data to confirm
Uncertain optimal starting thickness profile - recalled quarter-wave rule may not apply to this dual-band objective
Uncertain whether 20 layers is optimal vs fewer or more layers within the 24-layer limit
Si substrate absorption in target bands not recalled precisely - affects emissivity calculation
No literature validation that this material pair is optimal for thermophotovoltaic emitter applications
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar dielectric stack on Si substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat) (alternating, starting with HfO2, 20 layers total). Optimize all 20 layer thicknesses individually. Target: maximize emissivity in 8000-13000 nm wavelength band, minimize emissivity in 3000-5000 nm wavelength band. Use thickness perturbation bound of ±0.15% and quadratic penalty weight of 0.025. Materials: hfo2, SiO2 (Kischkat), si. Total layer count must not exceed 24 (fixed at 20 for this route).
revision_reason: Refinement based on iteration 14 results: reduced thickness perturbation bounds from ±0.2% to ±0.15% and increased quadratic penalty weight from 0.02 to 0.025 to enforce finer local exploration around the best candidate (target score 0.914) while maintaining convergence stability.
